Section 80C. Up to ₹1,50,000 a year of EPF, PPF, ELSS, life insurance premiums and some other savings comes off your income in the old regime. The new regime allows none.

Section 80D. Health insurance premiums come off your income in the old regime: up to ₹25,000 for you, your spouse and children, and ₹25,000 more for your parents. Each limit is ₹50,000 where someone covered is 60 or over.

Tax on income TDS does not cover, paid in four instalments by 15 June, 15 September, 15 December and 15 March: 15%, 45%, 75% and all of it. It applies only when the year's tax less TDS reaches ₹10,000.
Paying off loans, highest rate first. Pay every debt's minimum and put the rest of the month's budget on the debt with the highest rate, rolling a cleared debt's payment on to the next.
Consolidated Account Statement. A password-protected PDF from CAMS or KFintech that lists every mutual fund you hold across fund houses. The detailed one has every transaction.
Health and education cess. 4% of the tax and surcharge, in both regimes.
Cost to company. Everything an employer spends on you, including its PF contribution and gratuity, which are not paid to you each month.

Equity-linked savings scheme. An equity mutual fund whose units count toward the 80C limit and are locked in for three years from each investment. A gain on it is a long-term capital gain: 12.5% on what is above ₹1,25,000 in the year.
Money set aside for essential spending, counted in months of it. Pocket's target is 6 months.
Employees' Provident Fund. 12% of basic pay from you and 12% from your employer go in each month. The balance earns the interest rate EPFO declares each year.

The first year the corpus, projected with the SIP and its step-up, reaches the corpus that year's spending needs. With the SIP and the need both growing, it can come before the planned retirement date.

House rent allowance. The part of your pay meant for rent. In the old regime the exempt part is the least of three figures: the HRA received, the rent paid less 10% of basic, and 50% or 40% of basic by city.
Long-term capital gains. The gain on listed shares or equity funds held for more than 12 months. The first ₹1,25,000 a year is tax-free. The rest is taxed at 12.5%, plus cess.

A limit on the extra tax just above a threshold: at most the income above it. Above the new regime's ₹12,00,000 rebate limit the tax is at most the income above ₹12,00,000. Surcharge thresholds work the same way.
Net asset value. The value of one unit of a mutual fund on a day. A statement's closing units at its NAV come to the market value it states.

What you own minus what you owe: bank balances, fixed deposits, shares and mutual funds at today's prices, EPF, PPF, NPS, and gold or property at a value you choose, less loans and card balances. Each figure needs a date.
National Pension System. A retirement account you pay into until retirement. Up to ₹50,000 a year of your own contribution, beyond 80C, comes off your income in the old regime under 80CCD(1B).
Public Provident Fund. A 15-year savings account at a bank or post office. It takes ₹500 to ₹1,50,000 a financial year, at an interest rate the government sets each quarter.

Rebate under section 87A. No tax at all on taxable income up to ₹12,00,000 in the new regime, and up to ₹5,00,000 in the old. With the standard deduction, a salary of up to ₹12,75,000 pays no tax in the new regime.
The months the emergency fund pays your essential spending with no income: the fund divided by a month's essential spending.
Systematic investment plan. A fixed amount put into a mutual fund on the same day each month.
Paying off loans, smallest balance first. Pay every debt's minimum and put the rest of the month's budget on the debt with the smallest balance, rolling a cleared debt's payment on to the next.
A flat amount taken off a salary before tax: ₹75,000 in the new regime, ₹50,000 in the old.
A SIP raised by a fixed percentage once a year to keep pace with pay rises. A 10% step-up on ₹10,000 a month makes it ₹11,000 a month in the second year and ₹12,100 in the third.
An addition to the tax on taxable income above ₹50 lakh: 10% of the tax, 15% above ₹1 crore, 25% above ₹2 crore, in both regimes; above ₹5 crore, 37% in the old regime and 25% in the new.

Tax deducted at source. Income tax taken off your pay by your employer each month: a twelfth of the year's tax on the salary. It counts toward the year's tax, so only what TDS does not cover is left to pay.
The share of the corpus taken out in the first year of retirement, and then increased with inflation. 4% is a rule of thumb for the 'safe-withdrawal' rate, not a guarantee.

Extended internal rate of return. The annualised, money-weighted rate of return on a portfolio, counting each dated purchase on its own date. Pocket shows it once money has been invested for about six months.
Investments plus accounts minus liabilities, each open to its lines.
